title: Petnjica solidarity gathering in a coordinated Palestine solidarity action
scope: Local gathering reported as one of coordinated same-day gatherings in ten municipalities; no count is pooled across sites.
organizer: Petnjica citizens’ group; the Palestine Solidarity Movement helped organize.

state_target.target: Montenegrin politicians and institutions were urged to condemn genocide, respect international court decisions and heed a petition.
state_target.evidence: Speaker called on Montenegrin politicians not to ignore the public will and to condemn genocide.

demands_original: Support for civilians in Gaza; condemnation of crimes; respect for international court decisions; call for Montenegrin politicians to take a position.
participants_original: Support for civilians in Gaza; condemnation of crimes; respect for international court decisions; call for Montenegrin politicians to take a position.
threshold_50_evidence: The local article gives no headcount for Petnjica; no other city’s count is transferred or pooled.

start_date.summary: The local report dates the gathering to Aug. 15.

end_date.summary: The report describes an Aug. 15 gathering; precise end time is not stated.

location.summary: Public gathering at Divan bašta in central Petnjica.

scope.summary: One local Petnjica gathering, which the report connects to coordinated gatherings across ten municipalities.

organizer.summary: Local citizens’ group organized; national movement helped.

state_target.summary: Speaker called on Montenegrin politicians not to ignore the public will and to condemn genocide.

demands.summary: Support for Palestinian civilians and international law; domestic political action requested.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No simultaneous count at the Petnjica location; ten participating municipalities do not establish a local threshold.

state_response.summary: No domestic state response to this local gathering documented.

notes: This is one local site within a reported coordinated campaign. Do not infer a 50-person local gathering from ten municipalities or an upcoming Sep. 14 Podgorica protest.
open_questions: What was the simultaneous attendance in Petnjica?
Can the exact common organizer and action scope across municipalities be established without pooling local attendance?

title: ŽICG employee rail-service stoppage and transport blockade, exact public-action status unresolved
location: Railway infrastructure/transport operations in Montenegro; exact gathering site unknown.
scope: Search-only result describes a multi-day stoppage by employees of the state railway infrastructure company.
organizer: ŽICG dispatchers and rail employees, according to search headers; formal organizer not established.

state_target.target: Search result refers to ŽICG management and talks with the transport ministry, but a public state-policy demand is not body-verified.
state_target.evidence: Talks involve management and the Ministry of Transport, but the exact target of the worker action is unclear from headers.

demands_original: Search headers report demands for higher salaries and stopped work/blockade; exact demand addressee and public action form remain unverified.
participants_original: Search headers report demands for higher salaries and stopped work/blockade; exact demand addressee and public action form remain unverified.
threshold_50_evidence: Search result reports more than 80/nearly 90 employees, but that is a workforce count, not proof of 50 gathered participants.

start_date.summary: Search result reports the stoppage began Friday Aug. 22 and continued into its fourth day.

location.summary: Rail service/lines are described; specific gathering location is not established.

organizer.summary: Employees in railway dispatch roles are identified; organizer not established.

demands.summary: Search header says employees seek higher pay.

participants_original.summary: Search result cites more than 80/nearly 90 employees, which is not event attendance.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No separate public-gathering count or evidence that workers took to the streets.

state_target.summary: Talks involve management and the Ministry of Transport, but the exact target of the worker action is unclear from headers.

notes: Retain only as a search-only lead. A workplace stoppage/transport disruption is not automatically a qualifying public protest; do not infer turnout from staffing numbers.
open_questions: Did workers hold a public gathering or street action, rather than only suspending work?
What was the simultaneous attendance at any public action and was the demand linked to state policy?
